I found a 100% open‑source alternative to DeepWiki!

Open DeepWiki turns any public repository into a wiki‑style knowledge base with clear documentation, beautiful architectural diagrams, and a conversational AI assistant.

Key Features:

• Instant Documentation: Convert any GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket repo into a wiki in seconds
• Private Repository Support: Securely connect private repos using personal access tokens
• Smart Analysis: AI-powered understanding of code relationships and structure
• Beautiful Diagrams: Auto-generated Mermaid diagrams for clarity
• Easy Navigation: Simple, intuitive interface for exploring repositories
• Ask Feature: Chat with your repository using RAG-powered AI for accurate answers
• DeepResearch: Multi-turn research for exploring complex topics in depth

It’s 100% Open Source.

author: Rajesh Padavala
headline: Integration Engineer
text:
Interesting Data Engineering Interview Scenario!
During my recent interview with Deloitte for a Data Engineer role, I was asked a very practical and thought-provoking SQL challenge that I’d love to share with the community:

📊 Scenario:
You are given two tables:

Emp1: Contains employee ID and name
Emp2: Contains employee ID, year, salary, and hours worked
(Note: Emp2 may have multiple records per employee because of the year column)

🎯 Objective:
For each employee:

Calculate the total hours worked from Emp2.

Based on the number of records in Emp2 for each employee:

If odd, pick the middle record's salary (based on year).

If even, split records into two halves and pick the last record from each half.

📌 It was a great test of logical thinking, row-level manipulation, and use of window functions.
